newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL - BROADWAY JOE HANDICAPS SUPER BOWL QUARTERBACKS.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL - BROADWAY JOE HANDICAPS SUPER BOWL QUARTERBACKS.

text.p: Former Super Bowl hero Joe Namath may be too old to play in the National Fooball League these days, but he hasn't lost any of the cockiness that made him "Broadway Joe" in the late 1960s.
"I could throw better than both (Drew) Bledsoe and Brett Favre," Namath said earlier this week when asked to handicap the Super Bowl XXXI quarterbacks.

Namath, notorious for his playboy lifestyle in his days with the New York Jets, sealed his place in Super Bowl folklore from the side of a swimming pool. Stretched out on a lounge chair, dressed in swimming trunks, Namath guaranteed victory for his Jets over the mighty Baltimore Colts in Super Bowl III.
He then went out and made good on his brash pronouncement.
The 53-year-old Namath was in New Orleans on Super Bowl-related business and not at all reluctant to share his opinion of this year's quarterbacks.
"Bledsoe has had to put up with a lot with Bill Parcells as head coach and Ray Perkins as offensive coordinator.
"He had to mature and grow up fast with those two. However, he's still a kid, a pup," Namath said of the 24-year-old New England Patriots signal caller.
"In comparison, Brett Favre is a hardened veteran. Playing Dallas in the playoffs can do that to you," Namath said of Green Bay's 27-year-old gunslinger and two-time NFL Most Valuable Player.
Namath didn't think Favre's habit of getting off to shaky starts would hurt him Sunday.
"Being nervous before the game is normal. If you don't get butterflies before a championship game there is something wrong," Namath said.
"Being nervous and being tight are different. Favre gets nervous early, then settles in. You have to handle that and not be so up that you can't play."
Namath, whose Jets were double-digit underdogs in 1969, believes a 14-point slight by oddsmakers could help the Patriots.
"We didn't like hearing that the Baltimore Colts were going to kick our backsides. It irritates and aggravates the players and I think Parcells can use that with the Patriots," he said.
Namath said he always roots for the underdogs, but if he had to pick between Bledsoe and Favre -- "I guess Favre because he is the hardened veteran."
